desc: Establish the fixed-pair counting identity: total over all arrangements = C(N-2, k-2) * (sum of Manhattan distances over all unordered cell pairs), with N=m*n.
Derive closed forms for the 1-D geometric sums: sum_{i<j}|i-j| over 0..L-1 equals (L-1)*L*(L+1)/6; cell-level row sum is n^2 times this with L=m, column sum is m^2 times this with L=n.
Implement `distanceSum`: precompute factorials/inverse factorials up to N, compute C(N-2, k-2) mod p, compute S = n^2*rowSum + m^2*colSum mod p, multiply and return; handle k=2 and k=N.
Verify against the two provided examples and brute-force enumeration on small (m,n,k) cases including boundaries k=2, k=N, and m=1 or n=1.
Switch away from enumeration/cut-DP/generating-function approaches in favor of the closed-form symmetry reduction.
